text: Skills Hub 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的 Agent Skills 技能中心插件。它通过原生侧边栏入口和中心栏面板接入界面，由主机端路由提供数据与文件操作。用户可以搜索 SkillHub、skills.sh 和 GitHub 技能来源，预览技能正文和文件清单；也可以浏览已加载技能、编辑技能内容、切换启用状态、创建技能，并把市场技能安装到用户或项目技能目录。面板提供英语和简体中文界面，适合希望在 DSH 中集中发现和维护技能的用户。使用需要 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 或更高版本；代码未声明必需 API 密钥。

Skills Hub adds an Agent Skills panel to DSH web. Search SkillHub, skills.sh, and GitHub; preview and manage skills; toggle invocation; create skills; and install them into user or project directories. It supports English and Simplified Chinese and requires DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer.

**Skills Hub** 的功能「技能市场搜索」：在面板的市场标签中按关键词搜索在线技能来源，并查看匹配条目。 通过面板对应标签或操作触发。
**Skills Hub** 的功能「预览技能」：打开技能详情，查看技能正文、元数据及文件清单，再决定后续操作。 通过面板对应标签或操作触发。
**Skills Hub** 的功能「本地技能管理」：列出本地及运行时技能，并支持编辑、启停和删除等管理操作。 通过面板对应标签或操作触发。
**Skills Hub** 的功能「创建技能」：将新技能写入用户级或当前项目的技能根目录。 通过面板对应标签或操作触发。
**Skills Hub** 的功能「安装市场技能」：选择用户或项目目录，把市场技能文件安装到相应技能根目录。 通过面板对应标签或操作触发。

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · @wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub：**Skills Hub** is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that adds a native, first-class panel to the web GUI for discovering, installing, and managing Agent Skills.

It ships three capabilities in one panel:

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · @wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub：The panel reads the official skill roots (`<project>/.dsh/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, plus any configured `customSkillDirs`) and merges the host's skill registry on top, so what the panel displays is exactly what the model receives.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · From a local checkout (link install)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path-to-this-repo>
```

Restart the DSH service. The sidebar then shows a **Skills Hub** entry; selecting it opens the panel in the center column.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Market tab：Type a query and press Enter. The source picker to the left of the search field selects which registry the search asks; the choice applies to the next search, so results always match the query that produced them.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Market tab：Long result lists load the next page automatically as you scroll, with an explicit "load more" button as the keyboard/click target. Selecting a skill's name opens a detail dialog rendered by the shell's own markdown renderer — the skill reads exactly as it does in a conversation — alongside its file list and total size.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Installing from the market：The detail dialog carries the install action. A skill is installed **after** its body has been read, so the licence line and the file list sit on the same screen as the button. Installing asks twice: the target root (user `~/.dsh/skills`, shared by every project, or the current project's `.dsh/skills`), then a confirmation that states the licence situation at the moment of decision.

The install itself is engineered to fail cleanly:

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Installing from the market：- **Staged then renamed.** Files land in a staging directory beside the target and the directory is renamed into place only when every file arrived. A failed or cancelled install leaves the previous state of the disk untouched — no half-written skill the model could later load.
- **Collision is an error.** An existing skill with the same name is never silently replaced (the panel answers 409; updating an installed skill is M4's job).
- **Bounded.** Per-file 2 MB, 16 MB total, 200 files, and every manifest path is validated against a strict relative-path grammar before anything is written.
- **Provenance travels with the skill.** A `.skills-hub.json` record inside the installed directory names the market id, the source, the licence at install time and the timestamp — the anchor M4's update checks read back.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Installing from the market：**Licences are stated, never laundered.** Every result row declares its licence: declared ones show it (MIT, GPL-3.0, …); undeclared ones show *No licence declared*. In a sampled catalogue more than half of the entries declare none, and that is a fact a user needs before deciding to copy a skill to disk.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · My Skills tab：Skills are grouped by provenance (project, user, plugin providers, runtime registration). A skill backed by a file can be enabled or disabled — the toggle rewrites `disable-model-invocation` in its frontmatter — edited, or deleted. Skills registered by plugins at runtime have no file on disk; the panel says so once, per group, instead of decorating every row, and their enable state is stored in the panel's own configuration.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Preview：Every skill can be previewed, including bundled and runtime-registered ones that have no `SKILL.md` on disk — the host falls back to the runtime skill registry for those, and the dialog labels the source honestly ("from file" / "from skill registry"). Frontmatter fields are shown as a definition list above the body and are never mixed into the markdown, because a leading `---` fence is a thematic break in GFM and would mangle the YAML into headings and stray prose.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Configuration：Plugin config (profile patch):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch; `false` mounts no routes. |
| `githubProxies` | `string[]` | built-in chain | Accelerator prefixes for GitHub raw content, tried in order; include `""` to try direct first. |
| `customSkillDirs` | `string[]` | `[]` | Additional skill root directories to scan. |
| `dshHome` | `string` | `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh` | Override for the user config root. |

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Security model：- **Every route sits behind the shared loopback fence** (socket address + `Host` header + browser same-origin markers). An unpaired LAN client receives `403 forbidden: loopback-only` before any skill file is touched. When `dsh-remote-web-ui` is loaded, a live paired-device cookie is an additional allow path; unpaired and revoked devices still receive 403.
- **A client-submitted `path` is only an identity claim.** Before touching any file, the host re-scans and requires the same skill name to resolve to that exact path. A project skill that disappeared can therefore never be redirected onto a same-named user skill, and the routes cannot be used to read or write an arbitrary path.
- **The browser never sends a URL.** Market requests carry only the opaque skill id the host issued; repositories, refs, directories and file paths are re-derived host-side, and the id grammar is validated segment by segment, so a path traversal is rejected before it can reach any fetch.
- **Remote fetching happens only in the host half**, behind the trust fence. The unauthenticated GitHub API allows 60 requests/hour, so only discovery (tree listing) touches

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Architecture：- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`, runs in the DSH server process) — serves the `/api/skills-hub/*` route family, owns all network access, file I/O, and the trust fence.
- **Client half** (`lib/client.js`, runs in the web GUI) — registers the sidebar entry and the center-column page through the shell's official slot seats (`sidebar.panellist` and the keyed `main` slot), so the shell owns the row box, active highlight and panel switching exactly as it does for its own Plugins and Schedule pages.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Architecture：The client is built only on the host's frozen browser module table (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-*`); every control is the official shared primitive (`Button`, `Switch`, `Input`, `Menu`, `Modal`, `MarkdownText`, …) — nothing is hand-drawn. Registration failures are logged and degrade the panel; they never fail the GUI's boot.

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck        # tsc --noEmit
pnpm build            # tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsdown
```

Test suites (run with `node tests/<file>.mjs`):

@wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub README · Development：| Suite | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `m0-smoke.mjs` | Loads both bundles the way the host does; asserts the loader contract, injected-require usage and route registration. |
| `m1-host.mjs` | Drives the route family against a real temporary skill tree: scan grading, write-route identity checks, symlink protection, fence denials. |
| `market.mjs` | Market layer with fake transports, zero network: aggregation, dedup, id grammar (incl. path-escape attempts), source contracts, installer staging/path-safety/provenance. |
| `ui-structure.mjs` | UI guards: official-primitives-only, card anatomy, scroll height chain — each negative-controlled. |
| `theme-tokens.mjs` | Verifies every referenced CSS custom property exists in the shipped theme, because an undefined token makes `var()` silently drop the whole declaration. |
| `market-live*.mjs`, `icon-live.mjs`, `install-live.mjs`, `tools/scroll-selftest.mjs` | Manual, live-network / real-browser smoke tests; not part of the automated gate. |
